domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The primary object is the DeepSeek R1/V3 foundation models—their MoE architecture, scaling-law context, test-time compute paradigm, emergent RL reasoning, and capability benchmarks. The discussion covers general-purpose foundation model architecture and training without a specific application vertical. Content spans V3 pre-training architecture, R1's four-stage post-training pipeline, and AIME/evaluation benchmarks. Assumes familiarity with MoE architectures, GRPO reinforcement learning, scaling laws, and distillation techniques. Recorded conference presentation at AI Engineer World's Fair structured as a paper club review of DeepSeek papers. Eight direct transcript evidence anchors with 'said_in_transcript' grade support the classification with specific quantitative claims.

summary: The session opens with a year-in-review of the Latent Space Paper Club, running weekly for 1.5+ years with ~100 attendees and peaking at 300 for DeepSeek V3. The major announcement is a curriculum-based "Test of Time" paper club covering 50-100 foundational papers organized by topic—GPT2, BERT, RNNs, LSTMs, pre-training, post-training, mid-training, scaling laws, Chinchilla, distillation, diffusion, optimization, voice, fine-tuning—with 3-4 papers presented each week followed by open discussion. The speaker clarifies this is a paper club, not a course: no active workshops or building, just presentations and discussions. Speakers will be invited, and the Discord already has a top 2025 papers list. The DeepSeek R1 0528 update is recapped: AIME 2024 improved from 70% to 87.5%, matching o3 and Gemini 2.5 Pro. Reasoning doubled from ~12,000 to ~25,000 tokens through additional RL, with native function calling, JSON outputs, and reduced hallucination. A new Qwen 3 8B distillation from updated R1 matches Qwen 3's 235B thinking model, is on par with Gemini 2.5 flash thinking and o3 mini, and is better than Qwen 32B—all open source and runnable on a laptop. The speaker emphasizes these are not R2 releases but mini refreshes. The original DeepSeek V3/R1 paper is contextualized within scaling law evolution. R10, the pure RL reasoning model on V3 base, is strong at math/code but poor at readability and general tasks. R1 builds on R10 through a four-stage pipeline: cold start SFT, RL on verifiable hard questions, rejection sampling on 800K samples, and final RL for helpful/harmless behavior. Distillations are SFT-style from R1's thinking traces into Qwen and Llama families, all reaching GPT-4o-level performance. Aha moments emerge spontaneously from RL without explicit instruction. The session closes with acknowledgments to volunteers (Eugene, Era, R.J., Flo, Swyx) and a call to join the Discord, scan QR codes, and contribute.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Paper Club Year in Review & Future Plans
sections.summary: Reviews 1.5 years of weekly Paper Club sessions with ~100 average attendees. Announces the new Test of Time Paper Club: a curriculum-based second club covering 50-100 foundational papers across GPT2, BERT, RNNs, LSTMs, pre/post/mid-training, scaling laws, Chinchilla, distillation, diffusion, optimization, voice, and fine-tuning. 3-4 papers presented weekly with open discussion. Clarified as a paper club, not a course. Will include SF in-person and remote sections. Regular Wednesday paper club continues unchanged.

sections.title: DeepSeek R1 0528 Update & New Distillation
sections.summary: Covers the May 28th DeepSeek R1 update: AIME 2024 from 70% to 87.5%, matching o3/Gemini 2.5 Pro performance, doubling reasoning tokens from ~12,000 to ~25,000, adding native function calling, JSON outputs, and reduced hallucination. A new Qwen 3 8B distillation from the updated R1 matches Qwen 3's 235B thinking model. Speaker addresses benchmark overfitting concerns.

sections.title: Original DeepSeek V3/R1 Paper Overview & Test-Time Scaling Context
sections.summary: Recaps the original DeepSeek V3/R1 paper, contextualizing it within scaling law evolution: Chinchilla-optimal training → overtraining for inference → test-time compute. DeepSeek was the first open test-time scaling model that performed well. Key insight: pure RL (GRPO) on the V3 base developed reasoning without supervised data, producing emergent reflection and aha moments. R1 uses a four-stage pipeline: cold start SFT → reasoning RL → rejection sampling → RL polishing.

sections.title: R10 vs R1, Distillation Strategy & DeepSeek V3 Architecture
sections.summary: DeepSeek released two early models: R10, a pure RL reasoning model trained only on chain of thought from the V3 base (no SFT), which is strong at reasoning but not general assistant performance; and R1, which builds on R10's outputs through the four-stage pipeline. Distillations were taken from R1's thinking traces into Qwen and Llama models. Models are MIT-licensed open source with no training data or code. DeepSeek V3 is open-source GPT-4o quality: 671B total / 37B active, trained on 15T tokens with MLA and multi-token prediction, reportedly for $5M. R10 uses GRPO with verifiable rewards on the base model.

sections.title: Aha Moments & Emergent Reasoning from RL
sections.summary: Details the aha moment phenomenon with a direct paper quote: rather than explicitly teaching models how to solve problems, RL with the right incentives causes models to autonomously develop advanced problem-solving strategies. Shows a math example where the model pauses mid-reasoning with 'wait, wait, wait' and re-evaluates its approach. R10 recap: pure RL on base model for math and code produces strong reasoning but poor readability and multi-language issues (reasoning in Chinese). Microsoft and Qwen teams have published related scaling laws and thinking models.

sections.title: R1 Four-Stage Training Pipeline Details
sections.summary: Explains how R1 is built from R10 to become a useful chat assistant. Stage 1: cold start SFT with a couple thousand examples and human annotators for readability, using think tags. Stage 2: main RL on verifiable hard math/code questions. Stage 3: rejection sampling—generate completions, rank with reward model, fine-tune; 800,000 samples generated (600K reasoning, 200K general chat), following Llama 3's rejection sampling approach. Stage 4: final RL for general use—helpful, harmless, good reasoning, with human preference capture for nuanced responses. Result: model good at both chat and reasoning with emergent aha behaviors.

sections.title: DeepSeek R1 0528 Update Recap & Distillation Details
sections.summary: Recaps the May 28th R1 update: now reasoning twice as long, matching o3 and Gemini 2.5 Pro, with native function calling, JSON outputs, and less hallucination. AIME jumped 17.5%. New 8B distillation into Qwen 3 matches Qwen 235B reasoning model. Distillation is SFT-style (not RL) from R1's 25-30K token thinking traces into Qwen 1.5B/7B/14B/32B and Llama 8B/70B—all reaching GPT-4o-level performance. RL on Qwen 32B base for 10K steps performed worse than distillation, confirming cold start is needed. R1 distill on chat model outperformed Qwen's QWQ32B. Calls for community to do RL-based distillation from large models.

sections.title: Future Work, Limitations & Recap
sections.summary: Lists R1 limitations: worse than V3 at function calling, multi-turn, and JSON mode (fixed in 0528 update), language mixing issues, prompting sensitivity, and not much better at engineering tasks. Notes OpenAI researchers say scaffolding with reasoning models means labs are failing. Mentions open recreations by Hugging Face and Bespoke Labs. Quick recap of Paper Club and Test of Time announcement for new joiners (~100-200 people in audience).

sections.title: Test of Time Curriculum Details, Final Recap & Acknowledgments
sections.summary: Details the Test of Time Paper Club curriculum: covering GPT2, BERT, RNNs, LSTMs, pre/post/mid-training, scaling laws, Chinchilla, distillation, diffusion, optimization, voice, and fine-tuning, with 3-4 papers presented weekly plus open discussion. Clarified as a paper club, not a course. QR code shared for involvement and paper recommendations; Discord has a top 2025 papers list. Final recap of DeepSeek R1 0528: twice the reasoning, matching o3 and Gemini 2.5, native function calling, JSON, less hallucination. Qwen 3 8B distillation on par with Gemini 2.5 flash thinking and o3 mini, better than Qwen 32B, matching Qwen 235B reasoning. Emphasizes these are mini refreshes, not R2. Aha moments come from inference-time scaling rather than next-token prediction. Closes with acknowledgments to volunteers (Eugene, Era, R.J., Flo, Swyx) and the community.
